Building a self-contained diet dashboard

Source: vignettes/dashboard.Rmd
dashboard.Rmd

dv_build_html() writes a single HTML file with one page per predator, modeled on the diet dashboard built for the southern Gulf of St. Lawrence. The landing page shows one card per predator, with its stomach count and, if you give a length column, its length range. Each predator page shows the diet in up to three bands: distinct prey items, prey records (% of all records) and weight (% of total weight). Every band has the same layout: one sunburst for all the predator’s records, one row of sunbursts per covariate you choose, and, if you ask for them, crossed rows.

The chunks below are shown but not run, because they write files. They use the invented example table that ships with the package.

library(DietView)

dat <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "dietview_example.csv", package = "DietView"),
  na.strings = c("NA", "")
)
lin <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "dietview_example_lineage.csv", package = "DietView"),
  na.strings = c("NA", "")
)
spec <- dv_spec(
  predator       = "predator_species_common_name",
  predator_latin = "predator_species_latin_name",
  stomach        = "stomach_id",
  prey_id        = "aphia_id",
  prey_name      = "verified_name",
  weight         = "prey_weight",
  digestion      = "digestion_level_id",
  covariates     = c("period", "size_class", "size_bin", "region")
)
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lin)

The simplest dashboard

Name the output file yourself. By default the build stays offline, so the cards have no photo:

dv_build_html(prep, output = file.path(tempdir(), "diet_dashboard.html"))

Stratifying each band by covariates

strata picks the covariates that get their own row of sunbursts in every band. cross adds crossed rows: cross = list(c(inner, outer)) gives one row per level of outer, with one sunburst per level of inner in that row.

dv_build_html(
  prep,
  output = file.path(tempdir(), "diet_dashboard.html"),
  strata = c("period", "size_class", "size_bin"),
  cross  = list(c("size_bin", "period")),   # length bins within periods
  bands  = c("count", "occurrence", "weight"),
  length_col = "somatic_length_cm"
)

In bands, "count" is the distinct prey items band, "occurrence" the prey records band and "weight" the weight band. Crossing multiplies the number of panels: two covariates with four levels each give sixteen sunbursts per band.

Identification cards

Each predator card can show a photo and a short description. DietView looks for a photo in this order: a local file you name in species_info, a local file in image_dir named after the predator or its Latin name, then, if you ask for it, an openly licensed photo from iNaturalist (photo_source = "inaturalist") or from Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons (photo_source = "wikipedia"). The photo is embedded in the HTML file, so the file stays complete on its own. To control what is shown, supply your own description and photo:

info <- list(
  "Atlantic cod" = list(
    desc  = "Demersal gadid; feeds on fish and invertebrates.",
    photo = "images/atlantic_cod.jpg"
  )
)
dv_build_html(prep, output = file.path(tempdir(), "diet_dashboard.html"),
              species_info = info, image_dir = "images")

To fill the cards from iNaturalist, give the predators’ Latin names in the spec (predator_latin) and ask for that source:

dv_build_html(prep, output = file.path(tempdir(), "diet_dashboard.html"),
              photo_source = "inaturalist", image_dir = "images")

Only photos under CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA are used unless you widen licenses, and each card shows the photographer and the license, linked to the photo’s page. Check the credit line on each card before you share the file. The article on species cards gives the details.

Deploying to a folder

dv_deploy() calls dv_build_html() and writes the file into a folder of your choice, for example one served by your web platform. It returns the path.

dv_deploy(prep, file = "dietview_dashboard.html",
          dir = file.path(tempdir(), "outputs"),
          strata = c("period", "size_class", "size_bin"),
          cross  = list(c("size_bin", "period")),
          length_col = "somatic_length_cm")

The dashboard is a snapshot. It holds the data as they were when you built it, opens in any browser and needs neither R nor an internet connection.
